thread:
Lina: EdgeBox partner flagged an overbilling for May 31 UTC 23:00-23:59 window. They say their device-side aggregation uses local TZ and our hourly rollup used UTC leading to double-counting overlap. Can we confirm? cc @diego-platform @evan-metering
Diego: Can you paste the partner example payloads and the device aggregation timestamp field name?
Lina: Example snippet from partner: { device_id: 'edge-42', agg_start: '2025-05-31T18:00:00-05:00', agg_end: '2025-05-31T18:59:59-05:00', tokens: 12456 } They send hourly batches aligned to local wall-clock.
Evan: Our ingest pipeline normalizes to UTC by truncating to hour based on received agg_start. If partner already aligned to local hour and they cross DST boundary or timezone, we can get two different partner batches mapping into same UTC hour or adjacent hours depending on offsets.
Rachel: So the symptom is partner claims we charged both their device batch and our re-rolled hourly event?
Evan: Potentially. I see a pattern: for device_id edge-42 we have both raw_events with ts 2025-05-31T23:00:10Z and an aggregated event from their webhook which we also rolled into the same hour because their agg_start normalized to 23:00Z due to -05:00 offset. That could double-count if dedupe didn't tie them.
Lina: Partner provided sequence ids: seq=9876 for raw and seq=9876-agg for batch. They expected us to dedupe by device_id+seq but our doc only recommends idempotency_key on individual events, not batch suffixes.
Diego: Ops: can you pull the ingest logs for edge-42 around 2025-05-31T22:50Z-23:10Z and grep for seq strings? Also check the dedupe-table TTL and dedupe key shape.
ingest-bot: Run started: ingest-log-query job=inq-1774455000 params={device:edge-42, from:2025-05-31T22:50:00Z, to:2025-05-31T23:10:00Z}
Evan: Query results: Found raw_event id=evt-555 seq=9876 ts=2025-05-31T23:00:10Z, and batch_event id=batch-191 seq_root=9876 agg_tokens=12456 agg_start=2025-05-31T23:00:00Z. Dedupe key present only for evt-555 (idempotency=evt-555). batch-191 missing idempotency_key.
Rachel: Billing impact estimate? How many partners affected?
Evan: Quick scan: ~14 device_ids show similar pattern in that partner account. Total overcount ~3.2% of that day's usage; for the partner it's ~$430.
Diego: Root cause: SDK guidance mismatch + our ingest code assumed partner batches are non-overlapping and include idempotency_key. Fix paths: (A) update partner docs & schema to require batch idempotency_key and seq_root; (B) ingest change to prefer seq_root dedupe when present; (C) backfill/dedupe job to de-duplicate duplicate rollups for that partner for the affected day.
Lina: Partner already paused billing dispute until we confirm. They asked for timeline and remediation.
Evan: I'll open GH issue and a backfill job. Backfill will scan partner_namespace + date and collapse events where seq_root present, keeping raw_event preferred.
ingest-bot: Backfill queued: job_id=bf-1774455000-edgesdk status=queued
Diego: Ops SRE to add a monitoring rule: if webhook batches contain agg_start with timezone offset != Z then flag for manual review. Also add a dedupe-mismatch alert when batch_idempotency_key missing but seq_root present.
Rachel: I'll prepare a credit memo draft and partner-facing note explaining cause + remediation + expected credit. We should also offer a one-time courtesy credit for the friction.
Lina: Partner-facing reply draft: "Thanks — root cause: timezone-aware device batches mapped to UTC without robust dedupe keys, leading to a small double-count. We've queued a backfill and will apply a $430 credit. ETA 24h."
Evan: Backfill job started. Rough ETA 6h due to scanning device history.
Lina: Thanks team. Followups: 1) schema update PR + announce to partners, 2) ingest change to prefer seq_root dedupe, 3) backfill job + billing credit, 4) monitoring rules. I'll assign actions and update partner after backfill completes. :white_check_mark:
